sections.title: Responses: What They Answer, and Whether They Were Consumed
What a turn asks of the owner
AI ↔ AI Multi-Agent with Chain Depth
SIP Call → Unified process_inbound with Protocol Traces

links.scope: Closed-room inbound, direct record, direct send and response refusals; a hook closing its current pass; archived-room inbound refusal.
missing: Streaming, externally changed status, regeneration and replacement records are supplied by the complementary lifecycle link. Optional voice entry paths need their own capability evidence.

links.scope: Response and injected passes, deleted rooms, bound replacement records, streaming boundaries, member records and regeneration while the room closes.
missing: Optional voice/conference entry paths require capability-specific evidence. Internal read-count optimizations are permitted, not required, by §5.1.

links.scope: Five public transitions from all four room statuses, no-op/refusal state and notice stability, and organization checks before overdue timers.
missing: The public read matrix and retained-channel gates are supplied by the complementary lifecycle links. Optional voice paths need their own capability evidence.
Snapshot equality alone cannot prove absence of identical writes on every persistent backend; specialized effect tests retain that responsibility.

links.scope: Public history, bindings and member reads at all four room statuses, organization isolation, missing resources and timeline cursors.
missing: This read link does not by itself prove every retained-channel write gate; those are covered by the complementary refusal links. Optional voice session teardown is outside the Level 0 scope.

links.scope: Named timer-check scope, overdue timers before public transitions, explicit/message resumption, timer-setting activity preservation, and timer closure before inbound.
missing: The complementary timer link supplies direct gates, sweeps, cancellation and concurrent-write source evidence. Atomic persistent-store transactions and paused sender/group routing retain their separate store/routing evidence.

links.scope: Due timers at direct mutations and response passes; activity exclusions; inert checks; all-page scoped sweeps; cancellation and concurrent commits before and after the status write.
missing: The shared runner cannot force a store-write interleaving or caller cancellation; the specialized source tests and corresponding Rust runtime tests are required alongside these receipts. Atomic persistent-store commits and paused automatic routing are covered in the store/routing areas rather than certified by this timer link.

links.scope: Caller outcomes retain successful and refused provider receipts; clean sets store none, partial failures keep all target outcomes, excluding the source.
missing: Real provider adapters and cancellation exception forms are specialized tests. A scripted output is not a proof that a vendor accepted or rejected a send. Generic transport-provider parity is outside this bounded lot.

links.scope: Local tool-call composition: cumulative character counts, slot identity and order, size coalescing, terminal frames, retry/fallback isolation, visibility and absence of partial call persistence.
missing: Provider wire parsing, distributed executors and publication failures are not established by these scenarios.
Wall-clock coalescing is not covered here; forced consumer abandonment and cross-family order have separate native source evidence.
The rest of this broad clause, including all stored tool outcome combinations, remains outside this link.

links.scope: Public realtime observations when a composing turn is cancelled, exceeds its loop budget or its caller is abandoned.
missing: Does not establish every provider or distributed executor lifecycle, nor wall-clock coalescing.

links.scope: Chat Completions tool-call composition, through the actual provider decoder and public room bus on simulated HTTP responses.
missing: Does not establish every provider protocol, remote service behavior, distributed executor or publication failure.
Wall-clock coalescing and all other outcomes of this broad clause remain outside this source link.

links.scope: Replacement of literal copies of the standing-instructions header and its recognized bracketed opening in a participant request.
missing: Identity and Discussion integration are separate work; these assertions inspect prompt text, not returned model content or session identifiers.
The native received-RPC/abandoned-reader and late-response races are separate proofs and are not credited to these sequential scenarios.
No standalone-session, service backend, remote-executor or overall conformance-level claim follows from these assertions.

links.scope: A deferred turn's long answered input stays whole through one or two context overflows; later rounds build on the compacted request, keep call/result pairs and store the first long result while retaining recent results.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: A generation hook reconstructs a deferred turn's unchanged input. Emergency compaction keeps that entire input and later messages, and subsequent memory compactions and requests retain the same boundary.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: A real Discussion delays a turn while later messages arrive. Between tool rounds, compact receives only the history before the answered input; a returned summary preserves that input, the later messages, runtime notes and tool pairs, even after an emergency or initial-memory summary.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: A generation hook reconstructs a deferred turn's unchanged input, at the same position (identical questions included) or at a unique moved position. Between tool rounds the memory receives exactly the history before that input and the generation usage; its summary keeps the input, later messages, runtime notes and tool pairs whole.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: Full-value association of deferred inputs after generation hooks; exact protected context and empty memory history when ambiguous, explicit overflow failure without replay, subsequent tool results shortened only when eligible, and unchanged ordinary-turn behavior.
missing: Multipart input matching and deferred-tool reopening combined with ambiguous inputs are outside these shared scenarios.

links.scope: In-place mutation, replacement, mutation followed by copying and input removal preserve historical tool results and memory additions while shortening only earlier new results, in both generation modes.
missing: Other input transformations and emergency overflow are covered by separate shared scenarios.

links.scope: The public block-naming helper replaces selected framed blocks with their names, retaining surrounding text and caller-selected tag behavior.
missing: This pure-helper slice adds no shared scenario assertions or backend/runtime execution receipts; native execution is not inferred from source references.
The native long-input counterparts assert returned text, not the Python timing bound or asymptotic complexity.
Summary and compaction integration, other context renderers and complete Unicode text-safety parity are not completed by this public export.
Custom and empty tag sets are explicit caller options; this link does not claim they frame unselected text safely.
The normative source unit remains partial; approved text-normalization exclusions and media/realtime/remote execution boundaries are unchanged.

links.scope: Partial lifecycle and response outcomes around a host-native session invalidation: session identity, terminal errors, interruption markers and completion-hook absence. The Python reference additionally specifies bounded authorization and activity refusal; these shared assertions prepare the ACP area's later RFC amendment, without treating those recovery details as explicit clauses of the current RFC.
missing: This link does not cover the whole ACP channel. Full tool/thinking/plan publications, permission policy, standalone sessions, catch-up, instructions, usage provenance and public preparation cancellation remain separate contracts.

Native Rust tests establish actual room-lock contention and stream terminal/drop boundaries; they are not formal scenario execution receipts. They do not establish remote release acknowledgement before every following turn after cancellation.
The activity scenarios test only the prohibition of replay after an update or a permission request. They do not claim complete support for those update types.

links.scope: Public room cancellation during initial opening, required configuration and authorized reconstruction ends without prompting and preserves interrupted metadata. An already prompting room receives session/cancel and retains the agent's returned outcome. Idle and absent-session boolean results follow the Python API reference; they are not asserted as new normative clauses.
missing: Steering Cancel, detach and standalone sessions remain separate contracts. This link does not close the entire ACP requirement.
The suspended set_config_option RPC does not establish the later configuration-publication callback boundary; that Python source variant remains open.
The active-prompt scenario explicitly releases an agent response after cancellation. It does not guarantee that arbitrary agents promptly acknowledge cancellation.
Transport-start and final-cleanup boundaries have native regression tests, not shared scenario execution receipts. This link does not claim parity of activity counters during cleanup.
Permissions, complete notifications, room context and instructions, usage provenance and previously deferred shutdown cases are outside this link.

links.scope: Release of an active room preparation blocked in its initial MCP supplier when the ACP channel itself closes, before any session or prompt. The kit remains alive and the supplier gate is never released. No response completion is announced.
missing: Only initial room preparation blocked in the MCP supplier is covered here; standalone and other shutdown boundaries keep their separate contracts.

Close is distinct from the public cancel/steer operation: the observed turn-link error and absence of an ACP interrupted marker are recorded, without claiming the cancellation-marker clauses from this close scenario.
This link does not claim all requirements grouped in RK-6.4-037, or synchronous active-turn count changes before the consumer drains.

links.scope: Thoughts route to the session's current room turn after another room opened the connection. Reused sessions start fresh windows; error and abandoned consumption close the window without a response report. Public cancel of an engaged prompt preserves a subsequently returned cancelled response and its report.
missing: The two-room scenario is sequential; it does not establish concurrent prompt isolation.
Updates and permission callbacks with no active turn remain outside this proof.
Preparation cancellation, standalone sessions and the rest of RK-6.4-037 retain their separate contracts.

links.scope: Outstanding tools close on the tested terminal paths; sequential room prompts retain their room routing, and both report-hook modes see room metadata updated after prompt start.
missing: Per-room isolation is sequential here, not a concurrent prompt test.
Updates outside an active turn, standalone calls and permission callbacks remain separate.
Shared turn-record access from ACP hooks is handled in a separate following lot; this corpus does not prove it.

links.scope: Sequential room session setup, host setting precedence, stored configuration restoration, explicit close and setup refusal before prompting.
missing: Per-room MCP server sources, additional directories, reconnection and invalidated-session recovery are deferred.
Standalone sessions, detach, opening races and cancellation matrices are deferred; one native close-crossing check does not establish that whole matrix.
Remote executor loss and recovery are not demonstrated by local stored-state restoration.
Agent-originated configuration updates and ephemeral publication remain outside this link.
Rust results are retained as native and aggregate cargo logs, not formal execution receipts; exact warning text is not paired here.

links.scope: Public results and wire traces for shared room openings, independent rooms, settings during prompts, real transport loss and reapplication or refusal of host values.
missing: Background owner calls alone do not establish lock contention: four native Rust opening tests poll the actual channel work while session/new is unanswered; their logs are not formal scenario receipts.
Authorized invalidation/rebuild, standalone, per-room MCP sources and directories, detach/cancellation matrices and agent-originated publications remain separate contracts.
Local reconnection does not prove remote executor loss or recovery. Native retired-lock and cleanup-warning checks are retained in the implementation, not represented as scenario receipts.

links.scope: On an authorized rebuilt room session, default settings and host overrides are reapplied before prompting. Refusal of required configuration requests closure of the replacement and fails the turn without prompting it.
missing: Standalone setup, per-room MCP sources and remote executor replacement remain outside these assertions. This is local session reconstruction on one connection.
Configuration publication callbacks and agent-originated setting persistence are not established by these scenarios.

links.scope: Fixed and per-room synchronous/asynchronous MCP suppliers for room sessions. Complete ordered descriptors are declared at every opening; reuse avoids resolution, reconnect and authorized rebuild resolve again (including an empty list), and host-opened sessions are reused. Supplier errors and cancellation before session creation leave no fallback session or prompt; a held room supplier does not prevent another room from opening.
missing: Standalone session suppliers remain part of RMK-1655 and are not credited here.
No external MCP server is contacted; these assertions prove descriptor resolution and declaration, not server access or authorization.
The remainder of session setup in RK-6.4-038 keeps its separate links and outstanding contracts.
Python iterable materialization and the approved Rust callback/list language forms have native tests, not additional formal scenario receipts.

links.scope: Required channel settings and locally retained host choices requested on temporary ACP sessions before prompting, including a scripted refusal and reconnection; the declared MCP server and additional directories.
missing: Persistent and remote-executor configuration recovery, host-call races and every room-session setup case remain separate evidence.
These ordered wire assertions establish requested values and prompt/close behavior, not agent-side execution policy or successful application of a refused setting.

links.scope: Room detachment returns without waiting for the agent, closes idle or running room sessions, prevents initial preparations from prompting, forgets host values and does not retain late host settings. A fresh attachment opens a new room session while unrelated rooms keep theirs.
missing: Standalone detachment remains a distinct contract tracked by RMK-1655.
An injected failure of the public turn-backend control transport is distinct from local ACP detachment; generic state cleanup evidence does not prove that failure boundary.
The remaining permission and transient-progress clauses in RK-6.4-039 are outside this link.
Catch-up content and notification-publication boundaries have separate contracts; this lot establishes fresh sessions, not their complete room context.
Native lifecycle regressions do not create shared scenario execution receipts.

links.scope: ACP permissions with no external handler: actual reject option selection and cancellation fallback.
missing: Configured external handler dispatch and approval remain separate contracts.
This link does not establish detach behavior, filesystem/terminal support, or transient plan/tool progress in the same RFC source unit.

links.scope: Configured handler callbacks and actual ACP permission choices, including unsupported overrides and repeated decisions.
missing: This does not certify detachment, filesystem/terminal requests, plans, CUSTOM events or every ACP contract in this source unit.
Native lifecycle, concurrency, cancellation and standalone tests are separate proofs; no native or service-specific execution receipt is inferred.

links.scope: The exact texts of sequential ACP prompt attempts with standing application instructions, including absent/blank defaults, RPC failure, separate rooms, explicit close, transport reconnect and authorized session rebuild.
missing: Identity and Discussion integration are separate work; these assertions inspect prompt text, not returned model content or session identifiers.
The native received-RPC/abandoned-reader and late-response races are separate proofs and are not credited to these sequential scenarios.
No standalone-session, service backend, remote-executor or overall conformance-level claim follows from these assertions.

links.scope: ACP local identity reaches Discussion addressing, dispatch candidates and peer notes.
missing: Constructor-time handles, absent/empty/whitespace identity values and declaration.identity=None are separate native tests; these shared assertions do not certify those boundaries.
Standing instruction placement, recovery and first-prompt-only behavior have prior-lot evidence; no host UI, remote executor or complete identity contract is certified here.

links.scope: Scripted ACP Discussion turns carry runtime notes, expose the replacement marker for a copied header, reject an unissued mark, accept an empty addressed request and receive cancellation when held.
missing: Prompt substring assertions do not establish exact notes ordering, header uniqueness or mark lifetime; these have separate native tests.
The hold scenario covers a scripted open prompt, not cancellation while opening, an uncooperative server or a remote executor.

History catch-up, silent-answer suppression, every copied-header input source and the whole Discussion state machine remain separate evidence. No service-backend or overall conformance-level claim follows.

links.scope: Four public AI result fields and their text-turn boundaries: response tasks/observations, tool structured copy/outcome, next-round reads, outcome replay and compaction retention.
missing: The broad provider interface remains partial; context fields, served-call markers, vendor protocols and unrelated methods are outside this slice.
No automatic persistence of response tasks or observations is inferred. History intentionally omits the structured copy while replaying the recorded outcome.
Native Rust and specialized Python execution logs are retained separately; this link creates no scenario, backend or runtime execution receipt.

links.scope: AIContext room snapshots and outgoing target capability metadata, including empty targets, selection, intersections and preservation through hooks and interleaved tool rounds.
missing: The broad provider-interface unit remains partial; served-call markers and unrelated vendor/provider methods are outside this slice.
Capability fields are metadata only; this slice proves no media or realtime delivery.
The shared interleaving assertions do not claim all recent_events or author_register values; the native full-snapshot test supplies that separate evidence.
Native Rust executions are retained separately and create no backend/runtime execution receipt in this inventory.

links.scope: The public extract_tools helper projects ordered tool definitions and a mixed schema/object channel sends their observed fields to its provider.
missing: This pure-helper slice adds no shared scenario assertions or backend/runtime execution receipts; native test execution is not inferred from these source references.
The provider interface and handler-composition source units remain partial; this extraction slice does not complete their other paths.
Extra/external channel tools, media/realtime execution, remote executors and served MCP/skill consumers remain outside this slice.
Private validation/coercion witnesses support the Rust parser review but are not public Python evidence or execution receipts.
Rust uses typed ToolEntry variants and field errors rather than Python runtime protocol checks, object identity or aggregated Pydantic diagnostics.

links.scope: Active ACP tool and response callbacks share the turn record; pre-completion writes reach callers and MESSAGEs, with isolation between consecutive and overlapping room turns.
missing: No guarantee is made for writes after a MESSAGE was stored or the caller received its result.
Permission callbacks, updates outside a turn, standalone sessions and distant public executors remain separate contracts.
The returned cancelled stop reason and abandoning the reader are distinct native cases; this link does not establish every external cancellation path.

links.scope: All four access values, crossed with mute, for inbound and directly injected source events and for transport/intelligence targets.
missing: Buffered and streamed response permissions, regenerated answers and permission changes during an in-flight turn are not exhaustively mapped by this link.

links.scope: A statically muted readable transport or intelligence binding still receives the event and contributes tasks and observations.
missing: Streaming mute transitions, unread stream closure, output_muted and mute/unmute lifecycle semantics remain outside this link.

missing: Framework-created internal records and all non-public event producers are not covered by this public-door matrix.

links.scope: Public visibility inputs, committed text events and per-agent model context on the in-memory backend.
missing: EDIT/DELETE target visibility narrowing, non-text content and every refusal/reentry path remain outside this mapping.
Streaming permission changes and all memory summarizer inputs need separate proofs.

links.scope: Rules 1-3 and 5 for static bindings: source refusal, readable targets, retained target effects and self-skip. Visibility is all throughout these matrices.
missing: Rules 4 and 6-8 (visibility, derived bindings, revocation and reconstructed context) require separate mappings.
Rule 2 response paths, hooks changing permissions, streaming transitions and unbound sources are outside the matrices.
Rule 3 hook-returned effects on refused messages are outside this link.

links.scope: Rule 2 read-only/mute stream precedence and rule 8 refused/deleted reader history, live edits and unfiltered host histories.
missing: This does not cover every permission rule, live permission transitions during a stream, arbitrary memory providers or distributed stores. Hook contexts and pure structural views use specialized tests, not shared scenario observations.

links.scope: Empty-room indexes, consecutive per-room commits and counters, concurrent writers, hard-deletion gaps, and every major pipeline commit path.
missing: A persistent-store uniqueness constraint and atomic allocation across independent connection owners require specialized store tests, beyond the shared runner. The model compatibility check is specialized too; a scenario receipt does not execute it.

links.scope: Twelve sends with one key under one locked hook return the original id and content without consuming its ten-pass budget; a following fresh send still commits.
missing: Other budget entry points, off-lock adoption, task lifetimes and concurrent deadlines retain their own specialized tests and existing scenarios.

links.scope: An ACP tool observer posting through its captured local kit draws the active delivery cascade budget, without an additional ACP loop depth.
missing: The budget fixture is in-process: it calls its captured kit, not a remote TurnHost. Other-room posts, background work after contexts end and the remote host path are not exercised here.
The native context guard separately checks inherited depth and expired admission.

links.scope: Forty-five buffered answers and forty-five hook notices fit separate budgets of fifty. Exact turn counts and transport deliveries reject prematurely capped work.
missing: Streaming segments and notices above the hook cap are separate Python variants, not proven by this buffered case. Optional voice and orchestration paths and mutation-hook recursion remain outside this link.

links.scope: In-process ACP per-tool observers: live delivery draws a pass; a post after delivery ends starts independent work at depth zero.
missing: This broad unit also covers separate hook-call budgets, mutation loops, spawned work and optional realtime observers; these ACP cases do not establish all those paths.
No remote or Redis executor context is claimed. Historical receipts of the prior scenario revisions remain historical, not credited to the strengthened cases.

links.scope: ACP lifecycle and intermediate custom progress on an ordinary room tool call, with default and explicit tool-text settings.
missing: Other ephemeral event types and channel kinds retain their own coverage.
These two scenarios do not measure the preview length limit or an interrupted call.

links.scope: Static visibility restriction for active ACP thought publications, through either the binding or the triggering message's answer scope, on a second room sharing an already-open connection.
missing: Binding changes during the turn, writes after the turn, and other access/mute variants are not exercised here.
Tools, hooks and other ephemeral families retain their separate contracts.
Direct channel calls and a revocation during model generation are outside these two ACP scenarios.

links.scope: Tool start and end publications from a directly wired scripted AI channel, for an unrestricted trigger, a private trigger and a binding narrowed after admission.
missing: A bound turn and work continuing after the prompt, a deleted or recreated room, other permission changes and other ephemeral event families remain outside this scenario.

links.scope: The subscriber receives structural tool activity even when BEFORE_BROADCAST blocks the corresponding ACP room rows.
missing: This scenario does not cover answer-text publications, reasoning, hook modifications or other channels.

links.scope: Response visibility intersections, propagation through a two-agent cascade, buffered real-model streams, hook narrowing and depth-limit records.
missing: Transport-produced answers, instruction and delegation cascade boundaries, concurrent binding changes and every streamed tool-row path remain outside this link.

links.scope: Named executor hooks: refusal of invalid names/modes and collisions, stable equal-priority activation order and per-trigger replacement.
missing: This link does not establish every trigger, filter, off-lock ordering rule or distributed registration path of the broad clause.

links.scope: Timer hooks receive one final stored context, including activity committed after the status write.
missing: Other lifecycle triggers retain their separate evidence; this link covers timer contexts only. The concurrent interleaving is proven by specialized source/runtime tests, not by a shared scenario receipt.

links.scope: BEFORE_BROADCAST through process_inbound, including fail-open/fail-closed behavior where configured.
missing: Other SYNC triggers and wrong payload types; exception-specific logging is not exhaustively asserted.

missing: Other channel doors, pre-execution hook triggers and all exception classes are separate contracts.
Native lifecycle, concurrency, cancellation and standalone tests are separate proofs; no native or service-specific execution receipt is inferred.

links.scope: Provider-owned text call markers, pending controls, local-name collisions, per-occurrence reporting, mixed replay, bounded copies and stopped/cut report boundaries.
missing: AIChannel.external_tool_handler integration and its source-test variants remain open; the three excluded source functions receive no credit.
Media/realtime execution, remote executors and vendor gateways remain outside this text slice.
Cancellation before report context loads is reviewed by code reading only; the gated runtime test cuts during SYNC after the context has loaded.
The broad RFC source unit remains partial; local-handler result override rules and unrelated tool paths are not completed by provider-owned reports.
Native Rust logs are retained separately; no aggregate Rust/backend/runtime execution receipt is synthesized.

links.scope: No-handler external reports: SYNC chaining and ASYNC original outcome, including a report interrupted after its completed result.
missing: ExternalToolHandler policy and permission decisions are not covered.
This link does not credit local tool result replacement, structured-copy clearing or every hook error mode.

links.scope: Report-only SYNC rewrites reach the next SYNC hook while ASYNC observes the provider result.
missing: This does not certify local tool service dispatch, every HookResult form, or structured result replacement.
Native lifecycle, concurrency, cancellation and standalone tests are separate proofs; no native or service-specific execution receipt is inferred.

missing: AIChannel.external_tool_handler integration and its source-test variants remain open; the three excluded source functions receive no credit.
Media/realtime execution, remote executors and vendor gateways remain outside this text slice.

links.scope: Local AI handler copies reach result hooks and persisted end rows. Shared cases cover replacement, clearing, text-only rewrite, invalid copy normalization, withholding, unsuccessful outcomes, parallel calls and cancellation after a handler write.
missing: Other ON_TOOL_CALL requirements, external-agent reporting and every possible cancellation window are not established by this link.
Only initial handler-copy transmission is duplicated in streaming and non-streaming; every hook variant is not claimed in both modes.
MCP bounds, shared map aliases, kept tasks, exact empty dictionaries and private Python dispatcher/context fault injections have no shared execution credit here.

links.scope: Active ACP room calls refused without a handler, including unannounced calls and a call completed despite refusal.
missing: Custom handler decisions, decision failures, report failures, re-approval and callback overrides remain separate contracts.
No native test or service-specific execution is inferred; out-of-turn and standalone callbacks remain separate.

links.scope: Recorded ACP outcomes and hook callback counts for configured decisions and report overrides, including fixed failure envelopes, refused_but_ran, fallback when reporting raises before delegation, and no duplicate after delegation.
missing: No credit is claimed for Python dynamic keyword introspection, local AI or realtime execution, remote owners or all outcomes across every backend.
Native lifecycle, concurrency, cancellation and standalone tests are separate proofs; no native or service-specific execution receipt is inferred.

links.scope: Script unknown-skill and policy refusals, raised executor failures, plus AI shutdown reports preserving executed arguments and distinguishing unstarted calls.
missing: Only AI text script variants and the named shutdown boundaries are covered; other provider doors, all cancellation races, and the entire composite clause are not certified. Executor teardown error forms remain native API parity evidence in the lot checklist.

links.scope: AI text-channel human input: notification-independent answers, timeout precedence and refusal versus failure.
missing: Voice and conference doors; handler-native retention and lifecycle proofs are outside these shared assertions.

links.scope: BEFORE_BROADCAST cannot widen or clear an answer scope, write internal visibility or widen a framework internal record.
missing: Replacement identity, authority fields, instruction marks and every hook trigger remain outside this scope. Framework voice record creation is Level 3; its visibility protection is specialized source evidence.

links.scope: Injection pass ordering, off-lock collection, refusal before storage, authority and mutation recipients, next-turn history, plus specialized cancellation, late-failure and Python model-transport evidence.
missing: Rust realtime/model-transport ingestion is not implemented or exercised by this core lot. Python silent-ingestion source evidence is linked, but does not certify Rust voice conformance (RMK-333).
Gate refusal is sampled at duplicate detection and room closure, with timeout after collection; this does not exhaust every pre-storage gate or every mutation revalidation race.
The interleaving fixtures do not establish queue ordering or fairness for a distributed lock manager.

links.scope: An INSTRUCTION returned by BEFORE_BROADCAST is dropped before its own pass; ordinary injections, tasks and observations remain.
All fourteen Python SYNC trigger names in the generic engine, BEFORE_DELIVER and ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED end-to-end, and identity challenge exceptions. Rust implements ten of these trigger names.
missing: End-to-end warning assertions for each typed turn and voice caller remain outside this mapping. Rust has no BEFORE_BRIDGE_AUDIO, BEFORE_BRIDGE_VIDEO, ON_SPEAK_DECISION or ON_VISION_RESULT; the Python engine tests do not certify those Rust features.

links.scope: Named calls draw their room work budget before the inbound rate bucket and address callbacks. A cap refusal consumes no rate token; an already empty bucket does not mask the cap; a rate refusal still consumes one work unit.
missing: The rest of the inbound pipeline and its failure paths are outside this preflight slice.
Native tests are source references here; their executions and Rust local gates are retained separately, not treated as scenario execution receipts.

links.scope: Step 2 only: explicit/custom routing, room creation, scoped refusal, auto-attach defaults, correspondent record before hooks and re-routing.
missing: The rest of the inbound pipeline has separate links and is not completed here. Ordering at parse/identity/commit boundaries, lifecycle completion, locks and cancellation retain specialized tests and previous lots. No complete credit is claimed for this composite unit.

links.scope: Running and queued cascades are isolated, including a second room on the same channel; cancellation preserves transport delivery, the first reason and completed outcomes.
missing: Caller-task cancellation, Python async finalizer ordering, cancellation suppression, setup failure, handed-over turns and close deadlines require specialized proofs. links.scope: Fresh ACP turn sessions for standalone instructions, their declared scope, selected exact prompts, retirement, room-session preservation, catch-up and best-effort copy of current room configuration.
missing: These assertions cover the scripted ACP channel only; memory-provider and other intelligence-channel reads, Discussion and model-generated output are not certified.
Reader abandonment, exact cancellation boundaries, log contents and hook ordering are outside these assertions; no service-backend, remote-executor or overall conformance-level claim follows.

links.scope: A greeting and a streamed segment do not advance the delivered cursor while their transport waits; a later public send follows the held greeting.
missing: The source Python test also injects an internal lane plan directly. Multi-worker persistence and lock deadlines require the separate distributed suites; no performance bound is inferred.

missing: Other broadcast steps, capabilities, retries, rates, concurrent delivery and intelligence execution are covered separately or remain unmapped.

links.scope: Recipient contracts, access, mute, visibility, side effects, target delivery, transcoding and retained outcomes at the broadcast boundary.
missing: Provider-specific normalization remains specialized, with RMK-1392 retaining its existing corners. Broadcast concurrency is checked for twelve targets, not a throughput claim. Rate limiting, breaker state transitions and all retry policies retain specialized suites.

links.scope: The delivered event follows the recent-event window supplied to the target.
missing: No certification of every intelligence memory backend or provider history rendering.

links.scope: Deleted text and edited text are withheld from later model calls; specialized tests retain event identity and remove raw payloads and media edit content while hooks keep audit content.
